task: Find fraud and bribery allegations involving Adani Green Energy, including the US indictment

merged.claim: Hindenburg report of 2023-01-24 alleged group-wide accounting irregularities, stock manipulation and offshore shell entities; Adani Green shares fell about 43%; SEBI dismissed the allegations against Adani companies in September 2025.

c1.note: BBC confirms the 2023-01-24 Hindenburg report and SEBI's September 2025 dismissal of the allegations; the 43% AGEL fall and the 22 pending cases are plausible but not shown in the passages.

c2.note: The report says New Leaina held over $420M of AGEL shares (about 95% of its portfolio) as of June to September 2021, and this is an unadjudicated allegation.

c3.note: Hindenburg's 29 January 2023 reply states that Mauritius shareholders bailed out AGEL through two OFS deals and helped it avoid delisting; this is an allegation only.

c5.note: The only $7.8M figure in the report relates to Globe Textiles, so the INR 7.8 billion Adani Green offering amount appears conflated and is unsupported.

c6.note: The group-level accusation of a stock manipulation and accounting fraud scheme and Adani's rejection are confirmed; the $3B figure is not directly shown in the passages.

c7.note: The docket and press confirm the indictment dates, the $265M alleged bribes and the 2026-08-10 dismissal of Counts Two to Four with prejudice, with judgment reserved on Counts One and Five for the non-appearing defendants.

c8.note: The DOJ release and court order support the indictment of the three executives and the dismissal with prejudice, which was not a trial acquittal; AGEL was not a defendant.

c9.note: The court granted DOJ's Rule 48(a) motion on 2026-08-10 and the order does not rule on the merits.

c10.note: The DOJ release matches the five-count indictment and the more than $250M bribery allegation, and the court dismissed Counts Two, Three and Four on 2026-08-10.

c11.note: The charges, the company's non-party status and the dismissal of the fraud counts with prejudice are all confirmed.

c12.note: The unsealing date, the case number, the more than $250M alleged bribes and the charged defendants are confirmed; Adani Green was not a defendant.

c13.note: The 47-page order of 2026-08-10 dismissing Counts Two to Four with prejudice is confirmed; the 'puffery' attribution to the judge is not verified and may reflect DOJ's argument.

c14.note: SEC Litigation Release 26554 of 14 May 2026 confirms the consent judgments filed without admitting or denying; the $6M and $12M penalties are not shown in the excerpt but are plausible.

c15.note: The SEC notice lists 2026-08-10 as the qualifying judgment date and DSIJ reports the SEC matter was resolved by final judgment; the penalty amounts are not directly shown.

c16.note: The SEC complaint (24-cv-08080, filed 2024-11-20) and the 2026-08-10 consent judgments ($6M and $12M) are confirmed. Adani Green was not a defendant.

c17.note: The SEC release matches the bribery allegations, the $750M bond with more than $175M from US investors, and the 2026 penalties.

c18.note: The complaint named only Gautam and Sagar Adani as defendants and concerned the 2021 Adani Green bond offering.

c19.note: The final judgment on consent was entered 2026-08-10 without admission or denial, with $6M and $12M penalties and permanent injunctions. This is the case's current state.

c20.note: Case number, filing date, allegations and the bond-issuer role are all consistent with the SEC release.

c22.note: SEC v. Cabanes, No. 1:24-cv-08081, was filed 2024-11-20 on FCPA charges tied to the same scheme. He was a former Azure Power director, so the event is related to the group rather than Adani Green itself.

c23.note: The status is wrong. SEBI disposed of the show-cause notice in December 2025 without directions or penalty, so adjudication is not ongoing. The 'settlement applications withdrawn' wording is unsupported.

c24.note: The SEBI show-cause notice of 2023-11-10 was disposed of without directions, disgorgement or penalty in the December 2025 order.

c25.note: SEBI found the allegations against Pranav Adani and the Shahs unsustainable and disposed of the notice without directions.

c27.note: The SEBI settlement order of 2026-09-22 over the auditor peer-review certificate issue is confirmed. It is a regulatory settlement, not a bribery finding.

c31.note: The Warren letter is dated 2026-06-11. The Volkov blog confirms the 2026-05-18 Rule 48(a) motion and the reported $10B investment idea, and says Adani denies any quid pro quo. The April timing and the Giuffra link are not shown in the passages.

c32.note: The WNPS fundamental-rights petition was filed on 2024-05-16. It is an environmental and transparency challenge, not a bribery finding.

c33.note: Newswire on 2024-06-27 reports Ajith Perera alleging large-scale fraud and a loss of over a billion USD. This is a political allegation only.
